cards.title: HalOS Wallpapers
cards.body: A new app for every wallpaper you have: SAINT's living wallpaper, your Wallpaper Engine wallpapers and your pictures.
cards.details: It finds every Wallpaper Engine wallpaper Steam downloaded, on HalOS and on your Windows drive, and shows them with their previews and whether each is a scene, a video or a web wallpaper.
cards.how:
Open HalOS Wallpapers from the app menu, or say "open wallpapers".
Pick a wallpaper, choose a monitor (or all), then Apply.
On a dual-boot PC, choose Look on Windows drives to add the ones from Windows.
Scene and web wallpapers need Wallpaper Engine support: the app installs it with one click.

cards.title: Window animations you choose
cards.body: Pick how windows open, close, minimize and switch desktops, each at its own speed. Nothing changes until you press Save.
cards.details: Profiles bundle all four: SAINT, Supernova, Snappy, Calm and Off come built in, and you can make, rename and delete your own. The SAINT star now plays all the way through and shrinks evenly.
cards.how:
Settings > Animations. Choose a profile, or a window event and what it plays.
The preview shows every change; Try on a real window plays it once on a test window.
Save puts it on your windows; Revert goes back.

cards.title: SAINT Visualizer widget
cards.body: The SAINT logo and its visualizer on a clear background, over any wallpaper: a picture, a slideshow or Wallpaper Engine.
cards.details: It moves with SAINT's voice, the music playing, your microphone or a slow breath, as bars under the logo or a ring around it. Sound levels are read live on this PC; nothing is recorded.
cards.how:
Choose Try it (or Settings > Wallpaper > Add the visualizer as a widget).
Drag the widget and its edges to place and size it.
Right-click it > Configure for what it moves with, its style and colour.

cards.title: A wallpaper that listens
cards.body: The living wallpaper: a colour or gradient with the SAINT logo anywhere, glowing and moving with SAINT's voice, your music or the microphone.
cards.how:
Settings > Wallpaper: colours, logo size and place, bars or a ring, what it moves with, per monitor.
Use the glow colour as the accent everywhere, or make a slideshow from a folder of pictures.

cards.title: A new Files
cards.body: Tabs, every drive in the sidebar with how full it is, folder sizes worked out in the background, and search in plain words.

cards.title: Task Manager groups
cards.body: Apps are grouped with their helper processes, so you see what an app really uses and can end it in one go.

cards.title: Live downloads
cards.body: One place for everything that's downloading: browsers, Steam, Flatpak, updates and AI models, with speed and time left.

cards.title: Sound that fixes itself
cards.body: No sound, only a "Dummy Output", or the monitor's speakers missing? HalOS checks the sound after login and repairs it. Settings › Sound lists every output, routes each app, and plays on several at once.

cards.title: Start from another device
cards.body: The boot menu and Recovery list every disk and USB stick, and Windows, so you can start from any of them.

cards.title: SAINT updates in place
cards.body: SAINT updates itself without reinstalling HalOS, and if an update misbehaves, roll back to the previous one.

cards.title: An avatar with a life of its own
cards.body: SAINT's avatar wanders, sits on your windows, pops in to say hello and wears outfits you choose.

cards.title: Passwords
cards.body: Your logins in the system keyring: copy, fill in, one-time codes, and import from Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox or Bitwarden.
